about.notice: ShellyLanMan is an independent project. It started from ShellyScanner and is built on its basis, developed further on its own; it is not affiliated with ShellyScanner, and not affiliated with or endorsed by usnasoft or Shelly Group. Shelly is a trademark of its owner.
firstrun.title: Welcome to ShellyLanMan
firstrun.text: ShellyLanMan discovers, monitors and manages Shelly devices on your local network. It is based on ShellyScanner by usnasoft.
firstrun.authNote: UI authentication is off by default. You can set a password in Settings → Security; only run ShellyLanMan on a network you trust, or behind a reverse proxy with authentication.

sch.help:
Each line is a job: when it runs (time, or before/after sunrise or sunset, days, weekdays and months) and what it calls on the device.
The expression field can be edited directly (seconds minutes hours day month weekday).
● enables or disables a job on the device at once; the other changes are written with Apply.
Double-click a parameters field (or use the ▾ menu) to edit known parameters; ▶ runs the call now.
Load ... adds the jobs of a backup file; they are written with Apply.
chart.none.title: No devices ticked
chart.none.text: Tick one or more devices on Devices, Checklist or Firmware; the charts show the ticked devices.
chart.help.title: Help
chart.help:
The readings of the last 24 hours are kept by ShellyLanMan, so a chart starts with history; new readings are added as the devices are refreshed.
Drag over the chart to zoom in; drag with the mouse held to move the time window. While paused the mouse wheel zooms. Resume (▶) returns to the live view.
Ctrl+R changes the range, Ctrl+P pauses or resumes, Ctrl+C copies the image.
The CSV layout (series one after the other, or side by side) and the default graph are in Settings → General.
help.title: Help
help.devices.title: Devices table
help.devices:
Click a row to select it; Ctrl+click and Shift+click select several. Double-click opens the device information (or its web page, see Settings → General).
Ctrl+F goes to the filter, Ctrl+E clears it, Ctrl+S changes the filter column. The toolbar actions work on the selected devices.
help.settings.title: Devices settings
help.settings: Settings opens FW Update, Wi-Fi 1/2, restricted login, MQTT and other settings for the selected devices; each apply reports one result line per device. Changes for offline devices are queued (Deferred page).
help.checklist.title: Checklist
help.checklist: A row per device with the settings worth checking (eco mode, LED, logs, Bluetooth, access point, roaming, Wi-Fi, range extender, scripts, automatic firmware update). Right-click a cell for the actions of that column.
help.firmware.title: Firmware and local download
help.firmware: The devices check for new firmware themselves; tick stable or beta and press Update. The Shelly index column compares each device with Shelly's firmware index; ⚡ shows a QR code to download that firmware from ShellyLanMan with a phone, for updating a device through its own access point.
help.backup.title: Backup and restore
help.backup: Backups are kept by ShellyLanMan (Settings → Network, backups per device) and can be downloaded. Restore asks the same questions as ShellyScanner (other device, passwords, scripts) and needs a confirmation.
help.scheduler.title: Scheduler
help.scheduler: Jobs of Gen2+ devices, thermostat profiles of the Wall Display and rules of the BLU TRV. The ? button in the scheduler explains the editor.
help.scripts.title: Scripts and KVS
help.scripts: Scripts of Gen2+ devices: run, stop, enable, upload from a file or a backup, download and edit (the ? button in the editor lists the shortcuts). The KVS tab edits the key-value store.
help.charts.title: Charts
help.charts: Select devices and press Charts. ShellyLanMan keeps 24 hours of readings; see Help under the chart for zoom, pause and export.
update.help: Off by default. When on, the server asks GitHub once a day for the releases of ShellyLanMan; nothing else is sent.
about.what1: ShellyLanMan is a network-based tool for monitoring and managing Shelly IoT devices. It automatically discovers devices on the local network and shows key information such as Wi-Fi strength, cloud connectivity, uptime, temperature and meter readings. Devices can be controlled directly, and configuration backup and restore are available from the toolbar.
about.what2: Firmware management is built in, with a QR code for a quick download of the firmware, so you can update a device through the Shelly's own access point.
about.what3: An MCP server lets AI assistants such as Claude Code read and manage your devices, and as a Home Assistant app ShellyLanMan sits in Home Assistant's sidebar and adds its checks to your Shelly devices there.
about.dataValue: JSON files in the data volume, no database
about.free: ShellyLanMan is free and open source, and always will be. If it saves you time, a coffee (or a few tokens for coding) is welcome — and never expected.
about.basedOnSS: The starting point and the basis: the features, the terminology and the Shelly know-how come from ShellyScanner by {author}. ShellyLanMan started from it and has been developed further as a web application.
about.basedOnMD: {author} gave the idea, the inspiration and the basis of the look and feel with MikroDash.
about.basedOnSM: {author}'s Shelly-MCP was the model for ShellyLanMan's MCP server: its tools for AI assistants, the confirmation gates and scenes.
about.coffeeFor: Beyond the credits, {author} deserves a coffee too.
server.title: Ports
server.fromApp: Set in Home Assistant: Settings → Apps → ShellyLanMan → Configuration → port. Change it there; the app restarts.
server.fromEnv: Set by SHELLYLANMAN_PORT in docker-compose.yml (or docker run -e). Change it there and run docker compose up -d.
server.fromDefault: The default. To change it, set SHELLYLANMAN_PORT in docker-compose.yml (or docker run -e) and run docker compose up -d.
server.bridge: This is the port inside the container. With host networking it is the port on the host; in bridge mode (-p 8095:3082) the left number is the one on the host.
server.ingressHow: Chosen by Home Assistant (a free port); nothing to set.
server.mcpLocal: Local address for Home Assistant (MCP, integration)
server.mcpLocalHow: Only reachable on this host. Switch it on or off and set its port in the app's Configuration: mcp_local, mcp_local_port.
mcp.intro: ShellyLanMan can serve AI assistants (Claude, local models) through the Model Context Protocol at /mcp: they can list and read your devices and, if you allow it, switch them. Everything stays on your LAN: devices are reached directly, never through the Shelly cloud.
mcp.access.control: Read and control (switches, lights, covers, thermostats, scenes, backup, reboot, firmware)
mcp.access.configure: Read, control and configure (also scripts, KVS, schedules, webhooks, virtual components, scenes, RPC calls, device login)
mcp.accessHelp: Reboot, firmware updates, deletes, script code, RPC writes and device login also need the assistant to confirm explicitly. Every action is written to the log.
mcp.tokenSet: A token is set. It is shown only once; make a new one if you lost it (the old one then stops working).
mcp.tokenShown: Copy the token now: it is not shown again.
mcp.tokenConfirm: Make a new token? Assistants that use the current one lose access.
mcp.warn: The token gives access to your devices: keep it secret. Do not expose ShellyLanMan to the internet.
blu.title: Identify BLU devices
blu.intro: A BLU device that a gateway only relays does not tell its model in its normal messages. In pairing mode it does: a gateway listens for 90 seconds and shows every BLU device that answers. Nothing is added or changed on the device or the gateway.
blu.noGateway: No gateway that can listen is online (a Pro, Gen3 or Gen4 Shelly on mains power).
blu.step1: Stand next to the BLU device and press Start.
blu.step2one: Hold its button for more than 10 seconds, until the LED flashes blue (pairing mode).
blu.step2two: Hold two of its buttons at the same time for more than 10 seconds, until the LED flashes blue (pairing mode; one button held is only a normal "hold").
blu.step2any: Hold its button for more than 10 seconds until the LED flashes blue — on the RC Button 4 and the Wall Switch 4: two buttons at the same time.
blu.step3: The device appears below with its model; it leaves pairing mode by itself.
blu.none: No BLU device answered. Was it in pairing mode (LED flashing blue)? Try again, close to the gateway.
blu.col.name: Short name
blu.note: The model is stored in ShellyLanMan's archive, not on the device. A name for the device can be set under Notes.
login.wait: Too many wrong passwords. Try again in {s} s.
security.intro: A password protects ShellyLanMan's pages and API on its own port. There is one password, no user name. Programs such as the Home Assistant integration then use the MCP token (Settings → MCP).
security.ingress: In Home Assistant's sidebar no password is asked: Home Assistant's login applies there. The password protects the app's own port on your LAN.
security.noCurrent: Here in Home Assistant the current password is not needed to change or switch it off: you are logged in to Home Assistant.
security.ruleMore: Stronger with digits, punctuation and length
security.isOn: ShellyLanMan is protected with a password.
security.changed: Password changed. Other browsers have to log in again.
security.offText: Needs the current password. Afterwards anyone who can reach this address can use ShellyLanMan again.
security.offTextHa: Afterwards anyone who can reach the app's own port can use ShellyLanMan again.
security.reset: Forgotten? Start ShellyLanMan once with the environment variable SHELLYLANMAN_RESET_PASSWORD=1: the password is removed. Then remove the variable again.
log.hint: ShellyLanMan's own log: the last 1000 lines since it started (information, warnings and errors). It is kept in memory only and gone after a restart. The devices' own logs are under Checklist → Logs.
log.pauseTip: Stop adding new lines to the list (they are kept)
log.clearTip: Hide the lines up to now; new lines still appear
sch.testConfirm: {method} restarts, updates or changes {device} in a way that is hard to undo. Run it now?
apw.title: Update firmware through the access point
apw.openTip: For a device that cannot update itself, or that ShellyLanMan does not know: a phone does it through the device's own Wi-Fi access point
apw.which.fromList: The update goes through this device's own access point.
apw.which.intro: Which Shelly? Give the name of its own Wi-Fi network as your phone shows it, for example ShellyPlus2PM-A8032AB636EC or shellyplug-s-80646F838136, or the MAC address of a device in the list.
apw.which.name: Access point name or MAC
apw.which.inList: This device is in your list: {name}
apw.which.unknown: The model cannot be read from this name. Choose it:
apw.file.intro: Do this first, with your phone on your home network: once it has joined the device's access point it can no longer reach ShellyLanMan. Scan the code or open the link, and keep the downloaded file.
apw.join.intro: Now join the device's own Wi-Fi network with your phone.
apw.join.qrAlt: QR code that joins the device's access point
apw.join.open: The network is open: it has no password. Scan the code with the phone's camera.
apw.join.protected: This access point has a password: join it by hand.
apw.join.off: The access point of this device is switched off.
apw.join.assumed: This is the device's default name, not read from the device (it could not be reached). Check the name your phone shows.
apw.page.intro: With the phone on that network, open the device's page.
apw.page.qrAlt: QR code of the device's address
apw.page.steps: In the page: Settings → Firmware, upload the file you saved and wait until the device has restarted. Keep the phone on the access point until it has finished; then put it back on your own network.
apw.wait.intro: ShellyLanMan is waiting for the device to come back on your network.
apw.wait.version: It now runs {current}; the file you downloaded was {target}.
apw.wait.notListed: A device that is not in your list is found by the scan once it is on your network; use Rescan if it takes long.
apw.wait.noId: This access point's name carries no full MAC address, so ShellyLanMan cannot tell which device it is. When the update is done, press Rescan on the Devices page.
